newsitem.title: CHINA: China frees Warburg employee after probe.
newsitem.headline: China frees Warburg employee after probe.

text.p: China has freed an employee of Swiss-owned SBC Warburg detained one month ago on suspicion of leaking state secrets, securities industries sources said on Thursday.
Ye Shu, a Chinese national working for the Beijing office of the securities firm, was released recently, they said.
Officials at the company's Beijing office and Hong Kong regional headquarters declined comment.
SBC Warburg is a unit of Swiss Bank Corp .
Ye was believed to have been detained on suspicion of having played a role in preparing materials for company clients on the trend of China's currency, the renminbi, the sources said.
They said the documents were said to have been based on official materials of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, which referred to a possible devaluation of the currency late next year.
China's broad definition of state secrets includes economic and financial information -- much of which would be considered public information in the West.
A China-born journalist working for a Hong Kong newspaper was jailed for 12 years in 1994 for allegedly leaking state secrets, believed to have been reports on interest rate trends and gold sales.
Earlier this year, Beijing detained a Chinese national employed by Royal Dutch/Shell Group on what was believed to be suspicion of obtaining state secrets linked to an oil refinery project.
The detentions have troubled many China-based foreign businessmen, who say they are concerned about what tasks they can give to their local employees without forcing them to break Chinese law.
